root.title: Photosynthesis
root.description: Photosynthesis is the process plants use to turn sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into sugar and oxygen.

children.title: Light
children.description: Sunlight provides the energy that drives photosynthesis. Chlorophyll absorbs mostly red and blue light.

children.title: Water
children.description: Water is absorbed by the roots. It is split to release oxygen and supply hydrogen for building sugar.

children.title: Carbon Dioxide
children.description: Carbon dioxide enters the leaves through small pores called stomata and provides the carbon used to make sugar.

children.title: Chloroplast
children.description: The chloroplast is the organelle where photosynthesis happens. It contains chlorophyll and the thylakoid membranes.

children.title: Glucose
children.description: Glucose is the sugar produced by photosynthesis. The plant uses it for energy and to build other molecules.

children.title: Oxygen
children.description: Oxygen is a by-product of splitting water during photosynthesis. It is released through the stomata into the air.
